title: Scaling the Scaling Logic: Agentic Meta-Synthesis of Logic Reasoning
claim: Prior data construction relies on humans for tasks and feedback; ours uses agents to automate the whole loop end-to-end.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, bottom progress arrow, agent loop wheel inset
description: Three rounded panels run left to right, with a long blue arrow beneath them showing progression. Each panel has a Task block (orange) and a Feedback block (green). Panel 1, Manual Annotation Logic (Prior), has Questions and Answer boxes, and Feedback marked Manual. Human badge icons sit on both blocks. Panel 2, Scaling the Logic (Prior), adds a Generator/Validator box with a Python logo and a stack of Questions, while Feedback is still Manual with human badges. Panel 3, Scaling the Scaling Logic (Ours), has stacked Tasks and robot icons in place of the humans. Its Feedback is Agentic. At the far right is a colorful pastel wheel with a lab-coat rabbit mascot and the labels Generate, Validate, Refine, Blind Review and Consensus, captioned Agentic feedback loop. Captions under each panel read Manual Annotation, Semi-Automatic Expert Synthesis and Full Automatic Agentic Synthesis.
caption: Paradigm Shifts in Logic Data Generation: From Manual Curation to Agentic Meta-Synthesis. Left: Traditional Manual Curation focuses on Task/QA pairs, where quality control and feedback rely heavily on humans. Middle: Code Synthesis introduces executable Generators/Validators, achieving partial automation but still requiring manual supervision. Right: Our Agentic Meta-Synthesis enables fully automatic, end-to-end data production. Agents iteratively generate and validate task families (Generator + Validator) and instances, realizing the path from Manual $\rightarrow$ Semi-Automatic $\rightarrow$ Full-Automatic construction (Scaling the Scaling Logic).
abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is bottlenecked by data: existing synthesis pipelines rely on expert-written code or fixed templates, confining growth to instance-level perturbations. We shift the evolvable unit from problem instances to task-family specifications. SSLogic is an agentic meta-synthesis framework in which LLM agents iteratively author and refine executable Generator-Validator pairs inside a closed Generate-Validate-Refine loop, producing families with new rules and difficulty gradients rather than parameter variations of old ones. A Multi-Gate Validation Protocol -- multi-strategy consensus plus Adversarial Blind Review, where independent agents solve each instance by writing and executing code -- filters ill-posed tasks before they enter training. Starting from 400 seed families, two evolution rounds yield 953 families and 21,389 verifiable instances. Three converging comparisons (step-matched, token-matched, and size-controlled on external Enigmata data) consistently show higher training utility of evolved data, with gains of SynLogic +5.2, AIME25 +3.0, and BBH +5.5 on Enigmata. Fine-grained KORBench evaluation reveals selective improvements in logic (+13.2%) and operation (+9.6%), linking structural evolution to downstream gains.
